text:
```
I'm on a small team that just moved our CI to a new provider, and I want to post on LinkedIn about what we learned. The post should read like a real engineer wrote it on a normal afternoon, not like marketing copy or an AI summary. Here are the facts to work from:

<facts>
- Our team is small.
- We migrated our CI to a new provider.
- The buildbot dashboard came up during the migration. [Replace this line with one or two sentences on what happened with it and what you learned.]
- [Add one or two more lessons from the migration, if you have them.]
</facts>

Write one LinkedIn post of about 150 words, in first person, using plain conversational sentences of mixed length. Include the buildbot dashboard story as a concrete detail. Use only the facts above. If something is missing, keep that part general rather than inventing numbers, names, or outcomes. Leave out hashtags and emojis, because they don't fit how I write. Avoid stock LinkedIn phrases such as "thrilled to share", "game-changer", and "key takeaways". End with one genuine question to the reader that invites them to share their own CI migration experience in the comments.

Reply with the post text only. Add no preamble, notes, or alternatives before or after it.
```
Effort: low (claude.ai: not settable here). It is a single short reply with little ambiguity.

**Assumptions**
- You didn't say what the buildbot dashboard thing was, so the prompt has a bracketed line for you to fill in. Without it, Claude can only stay vague on that point.
- The prompt has no lessons beyond the dashboard, so I added a second bracketed slot for one or two more.
- The prompt doesn't name the old or new CI provider. Add them if you want them in the post.
- I assumed first person, singular voice ("I"). If you want "we", change that in the prompt.

**Changes**
- The prompt opens with the situation and the reason for the post, then the task, the constraints and the output. (anthropic: best-practices, Be clear and direct)
- The facts sit in an XML-tagged block, and each constraint has a reason, such as no emojis because they don't fit your voice. (best-practices, Structure prompts with XML tags; Add context to improve performance)
- The constraints say what to do ("plain conversational sentences") and name the stock phrases to avoid, so the "not like an AI" request is concrete. (best-practices, Control the format of responses)
- The last line is an explicit stop condition: the post only, with nothing before or after it. (SKILL.md, chat prompts need a stop condition)

**Guidance**: cached 2026-10-06 13:10, so the sources were not fetched live this run. The target was `anthropic` (claude.ai chat). The guidance script defaulted to the flagship claude-fable-5-1, and I named no model. No flags were raised.
